question_text: Suppose $X$ is normally distributed with $\mathrm{P}(X \le 24) = 0.035$ and $\mathrm{P}(X \ge 33) = 0.262$. Find the mean and standard deviation of $X$ correct to 3 significant figures.

subparts.stem: Suppose $X$ is normally distributed with $\mathrm{P}(X \le 24) = 0.035$ and $\mathrm{P}(X \ge 33) = 0.262$. Find the mean and standard deviation of $X$ correct to 3 significant figures.

mark_breakdown.desc: Standardizing both given tail probabilities to form equations in terms of $\mu$ and $\sigma$
Setting up simultaneous linear equations for $\mu$ and $\sigma$

subparts.solution: $X \sim \text{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$ where we have to find $\mu$ and $\sigma$.\\We start by finding $z_1$ and $z_2$ which correspond to $x_1 = 24$ and $x_2 = 33$.\\Now $\text{P}(X \leqslant x_1) = 0.035$\\\begin{aligned} \therefore \text{P}\left(\frac{X - \mu}{\sigma} \leqslant \frac{24 - \mu}{\sigma}\right) &= 0.035 \\ \therefore \text{P}\left(Z \leqslant \frac{24 - \mu}{\sigma}\right) &= 0.035 \quad \left\{Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma}\right\} \\ \therefore z_1 = \frac{24 - \mu}{\sigma} &\approx -1.8119 \quad \left\{Z \sim \text{N}(0, 1^2)\right\} \\ \therefore 24 - \mu &\approx -1.8119\sigma \quad \dots (1) \end{aligned}\\and $\text{P}(X \geqslant x_2) = 0.262$\\\begin{aligned} \therefore \text{P}(X < x_2) &= 0.738 \\ \therefore \text{P}\left(\frac{X - \mu}{\sigma} < \frac{33 - \mu}{\sigma}\right) &= 0.738 \\ \therefore \text{P}\left(Z < \frac{33 - \mu}{\sigma}\right) &= 0.738 \quad \left\{Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma}\right\} \\ \therefore z_2 = \frac{33 - \mu}{\sigma} &\approx 0.6372 \quad \left\{Z \sim \text{N}(0, 1^2)\right\} \\ \therefore 33 - \mu &\approx 0.6372\sigma \quad \dots (2) \end{aligned}\\Solving (1) and (2) simultaneously, $\mu \approx 30.7$ and $\sigma \approx 3.67$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: When both $\mu$ and $\sigma$ are unknown, two conditions with given probabilities can be converted to standard normal $z$-scores to form a system of two linear equations in $\mu$ and $\sigma$.
step_by_step: Use the lower tail $\text{P}(X \leqslant 24) = 0.035$ with inverse normal to get $z_1 \approx -1.8119$, giving $24 - \mu = -1.8119\sigma$.
Convert the upper tail $\text{P}(X \geqslant 33) = 0.262$ into a lower tail cumulative probability: $\text{P}(X < 33) = 1 - 0.262 = 0.738$.
Use inverse normal on $0.738$ to find $z_2 \approx 0.6372$, giving $33 - \mu = 0.6372\sigma$.
Substitute $\sigma$ back into either equation to find $\mu \approx 30.7$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using the upper-tail probability directly in the standard inverse normal function without converting it to the cumulative left-tail area ($1 - p$).
